name: US Foods Holding Corp.
moat_justification: Weak-to-moderate moat, 4/10. US Foods is the second-largest U.S. broadline foodservice distributor (~10% share vs Sysco at ~17-18%), with a dense national distribution network, scale purchasing, private label, and value-added services driving per-case operating leverage. Against that: Sysco is larger with a demonstrated cost advantage (Morningstar assigns US Foods no moat), customers can multi-source with low switching costs, margins are thin (Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin 5.7%), and the business is exposed to restaurant cyclicality, labor and fuel costs. CAP = 7.2 years.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.1x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Solid #2 foodservice distributor, moat 4/10, but priced for much more than its owner's earnings deliver - weighted IRR 7.66% at $101.47, does not clear 15%; hurdle-clearing price is the weighted IV@15% of $40.28.
moat_for: Dense national distribution and route network
Diversified mix across independents, healthcare, hospitality and chains
Private label and value-added services (Pronto, MenuIQ)
Scale purchasing and per-case operating leverage
moat_against: Sysco is larger (~17-18% share) with a cost advantage; no demonstrated moat vs peers
Thin margins - Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin 5.7%
Labor, fuel and food-inflation pass-through risk
Restaurant cyclicality - chain case volume fell 1.5% in Q2 2026
